development_note: declared before any rustc or RustGM run of these files. Scratch probes of the provider lines with main's CLI (obj/parallel/nonnull/explore/p1) found three fences: a pattern field stops export with `source type form requires an explicitly supported transport row`; core's open, exclusive and alternative ranges need the RangeMin/RangeMax/RangeSub roles, which the exporter fences with `source range helper contract transport is not implemented`; and a const endpoint needs a module `const` item, which fails with `source declaration kind is outside the initial source profile`. So the provider carries NonNull, core's closed ranges and two authored closed ranges. Clients cannot build a pattern-typed value (no transmute transport) or call size_of (clients cannot declare intrinsics; body-less intrinsics do not export), so each accepted client binds `Opt::None` of one imported type
wire_rule: approved shapes. Type recipe tag 16, version 13 only: [16][u32 base][u8 kind]; kind 0 is `!null` with no operands over a tag-12 raw pointer base; kind 1 is a scalar range [u128 start][u128 end] of raw target-width bits over a tag-0 integer or char base; any other kind is `unknown source pattern constraint`. The consumer re-proves each pattern through the local interning: a range in source order through intern_scalar_range, a wrapped one split into `MIN..=end` and `start..=MAX` through intern_scalar_or. NonNull's diagnostic identity is role-table escape tag 254, [254][string "NonNull"][address], after the language rows and outside the policy's role range; the spelling comes from a closed table, and the consumer requires this provider's own module-owned struct. `rustc_nonnull_optimization_guaranteed` has no byte. No layout, niche or ABI fact travels
